descriptors.R: nominee of the party in office since 1921; the sitting President is not running again
descriptors.D: nominee of the party out of the presidency since 1921, which held it from 1913 to 1921

compile_desc.D: the party out of the presidency since 1921

others_line: Other candidates on some ballots, including a Socialist and a Workers (Communist) party nominee (answer "other").
never_name: Hoover, Al Smith, Curtis, Robinson, Norman Thomas, Foster, Coolidge, Harding or Wilson

slice_sources.men: 1920 and 1930 censuses interpolated to November 1928 (the 1930 "Mexican" race category folded back into white, as the 1940 census later recoded it); men 21+ outside the eleven Southern states, citizens only, American Indians included as citizens since the 1924 Indian Citizenship Act though some Western states still kept them from voting; calibrated to certified 1928 returns.
slice_sources.women: 1920–1930 interpolation to November 1928, women 21+ outside the South, all enfranchised by the Nineteenth Amendment; turnout from the carried-forward women-to-men ratio, calibrated to each state's 1928 vote.
slice_sources.south-white: 1920–1930 interpolation to November 1928, white adults (including Mexican-origin adults, listed separately in 1930) in the eleven former Confederate states; calibrated to certified 1928 returns.
slice_sources.black-south: 1920–1930 interpolation to November 1928, Black adults in the eleven former Confederate states; disfranchisement by poll tax, literacy test and the white primary continues, and the 1920 exclusion estimate is carried forward.
slice_sources.immigrants: 1920–1930 interpolation to November 1928, foreign-born white adults who were not naturalized; Arkansas, the last state to let aliens vote, ended it in 1926.

masks: the nominee of the party out of power
a New York City party organization
